key_insight: 3D coupled opto-electro-thermal simulations show that lead-free MgXS3 (X = Ti, Zr, Hf) chalcogenide perovskites can deliver high-efficiency, thermally robust solar cells when thickness, doping, defects, and BSF design are optimized.
engineering_relevance: This work provides device-design guidance for replacing toxic Pb-based absorbers with scalable, high-performance, thermally stable alternative perovskite architectures.
method: 3D finite-element COMSOL simulation with self-consistent optical generation, drift-diffusion transport, and heat transfer.
Modeled ZnSe/MgXS3/Sb2S3 solar-cell stacks under AM 1.5G 1-sun illumination.
Systematically varied absorber thickness, doping, defect density, and Sb2S3 back-surface-field effects.
evidence_signal: Optimized devices reached simulated PCEs of 28.18% (MgZrS3), 26.72% (MgTiS3), and 28.16% (MgHfS3), with corresponding VOC/JSC/FF values reported in the abstract.
watch_item: The results are simulation-based, so experimental fabrication, interface quality, and real defect distributions may reduce performance relative to the modeled case.
paper_title: Numerical exploration on unveiling the photovoltaic potential of MgXS3(X = Ti, Zr, Hf) chalcogenide perovskites
